prerequisites: Students must have a basic knowledge of programming.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have insight into the architecture of a computer and can explain the role and operation of the main components (processor, I/O devices, memory).
Students can read and write programs in a modern Instruction Set Architecture.
Students can manually translate a program in a higher-level programming language, e.g., C, to a concrete Instruction Set Architecture, e.g., RISC-V.
Students understand the different representation methods for numerical and non-numerical data in a computer and how operations are performed on them.
Students understand the functions of system software such as the compiler, linker, and loader, and the role they play in program execution.
Students understand how a processor can be implemented in hardware and can explain techniques that improve processor speed.
Students have insight into the memory hierarchy used by modern computer systems and in techniques used to efficiently use memory.

syllabus_topics: Part 1: The hardware/software interface: Instruction Set Architectures, system software
Part 3: Memory hierarchy: memory technologies, caches, memory management
Students gain practical experience writing programs in the RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture, and complete assignments that deepen understanding of concepts covered in this course.
assessment_rules: Evaluation is based on continuous assessment for the practicals and a concluding written exam during the examination period. A resit follows the same modalities as the first exam opportunity.
bibliography: Computer organization and design, RISC-V Edition, Patterson en Hennessy
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
